title: Power Display Tray Icon never runs on windows start up
author: francoteves

status.label: Needs startup-path diagnostics
status.detail: Manual launch works, but the report does not distinguish PowerDisplay process startup from notification-area icon registration.

next_action.label: Request focused startup evidence
next_action.reason: Identify whether Runner never starts PowerDisplay or the tray icon fails while the process is already running.

judgment.rationale: The report establishes the user-visible symptom and workaround, but current architecture has separate module-process startup and tray-icon registration paths that require different fixes.
evidence: The reporter says manually opening Power Display makes the tray icon remain available until the next Windows startup.
The only comment offers a Startup-folder shortcut workaround, not a diagnosis.
Current PowerDisplay module enablement starts PowerToys.PowerDisplay.exe, and that process separately calls Shell_NotifyIcon with startup retry handling.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for current-version startup state and a fresh diagnostic ZIP captured immediately after sign-in.

issue_context.summary: Power Display's tray icon is absent after Windows sign-in but appears and remains available after Power Display is opened manually.
known_information: The original report is from PowerToys 0.99.1 installed through auto-update.
Manual launch restores the icon for the remainder of the session.
Current source starts PowerDisplay from the module process manager and creates the tray icon inside PowerDisplay on launch.
TrayIconService already includes retry paths for Explorer not being ready during startup.
inferences: The module process may not start at sign-in, or it may run while initial tray registration and retry fail.
A Startup-folder shortcut masks both possibilities and should not be treated as the product fix.
issue_context.analysis: The requested evidence is narrowly aimed at the architecture boundary. A fresh archive immediately after sign-in is necessary because later manual launch changes the process and tray state.
initial_investigation: Inspected PowerDisplayModuleInterface process startup, PowerDisplay OnLaunched, and TrayIconService registration and retry logic.
Reviewed the full issue, workaround comment, labels, and timeline; no linked fix or duplicate is present.

information_gaps.information: Current-version state of PowerToys auto-start, Power Display enablement, tray-icon setting, and PowerDisplay process before manual launch
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes runner/module startup failure from notification-area registration failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: After signing in and before opening Power Display manually, confirm the three settings and whether PowerToys.PowerDisplay.exe is present in Task Manager.

information_gaps.information: Fresh Runner and PowerDisplay startup logs from the affected sign-in
information_gaps.why_needed: The logs show whether process launch, named-pipe connection, or Shell_NotifyIcon failed.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Immediately after reproducing at sign-in and before manual launch, add a comment containing /bugreport so the generated ZIP captures startup logs.

actions.label: Ask for Power Display startup evidence

comment.body: Thanks—the report establishes that manually opening Power Display restores its tray icon for the rest of the session, while the Startup-folder shortcut is only a workaround. Please retest on the latest stable or Preview build and, immediately after signing in but before opening Power Display manually, confirm that PowerToys itself auto-started, Power Display is enabled, **Show system tray icon** is enabled, and whether `PowerToys.PowerDisplay.exe` is already running in Task Manager. Then add a comment containing `/bugreport` so the generated ZIP captures the Runner and Power Display startup logs from that state.

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.
